source_text: {ΚΥΡ.} Εἰ δὲ δὴ καὶ ἐπ' αὐτόν τις τὸν ἀοίδιμον Ἰωσὴφ ἴοι, εὑρήσει παρέντα τῆς ἐπιεικείας οὐδὲν, ἐννενοηκότα δὲ ὅτι συνεργάσεται πρὸς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐπαμυνεῖ Θεὸς, εἰ παραιτοῖτο γενικῶς τὸ καταμολύνεσθαι δεῖν. Ἐξὸν γὰρ εὐημερεῖν καὶ κατευρύνεσθαι ταῖς τρυφαῖς, τοῖς τῆς νεότητος διαπύροις σκιρτήμασιν εἰς τὸ ἡδύ τε καὶ φίλον ἀνέντα τρέχειν, καὶ ἀνεπιπλήκτοις φέρεσθαι ταῖς ὁρμαῖς, τοῦτο μὲν οὐκ ἔδρα, πολλοῦ γε καὶ δεῖ, μοῖραν δὲ ὥσπερ ἐποιεῖτο κρείττονα τὴν παρὰ Θεῷ, καὶ τῆς ἐγκρατείας τοὺς πόνους προετίθει παντὸς τοῦ παραυτίκα καταπιαίνοντος. Ἤδει γὰρ ὅτι γλυκὺ μέν πώς ἐστιν ἐν ἀρχαῖς, τὸ σαρκὸς ἐρέθισμα, καὶ οἱονεὶ μέλιτι καταγοητεύει τὸν νοῦν, ὡς ἔν γε τούτοις ἡδονὴ, καταστρέφει γε μὴν εἰς τέλος οὐκέτι τὸ γλυκύ· ποιναὶ γὰρ εὐθὺς καὶ δίκαι, καὶ τί γὰρ οὐχὶ τῶν τοιῶνδε κακῶν, τῆς τοῦ πεπλημμεληκότος καταρτηθήσονται κεφαλῆς, βούλει λέγωμεν ὀλίγα ἄττα τῶν ἐπ' αὐτῷ γεγραμμένων; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} «Καὶ ἦν,» φησὶν, «Ἰωσὴφ καλὸς τῷ εἴδει, καὶ ὡραῖος τῇ ὄψει σφόδρα. Καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα, καὶ ἐπέβαλεν ἡ γυνὴ τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς ἐπὶ Ἰωσὴφ, καὶ εἶπεν· Κοιμήθητι μετ' ἐμοῦ. Ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἤθελεν, εἶπε δὲ τῇ γυναικὶ τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ· Εἰ ὁ κύριός μου οὐ γινώσκει δι' ἐμὲ οὐδὲν ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἐστὶν αὐτῷ, ἔδωκεν εἰς τὰς χεῖράς μου, καὶ οὐχ ὑπερέχει ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ταύτῃ οὐθὲν ἐμοῦ, οὐδὲ ὑπεξῄρηται ἀπ' ἐμοῦ οὐδὲν, πλὴν σοῦ, διὰ τὸ σὲ γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ εἶναι, καὶ πῶς ποιήσω τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ πονηρὸν τοῦτο, καὶ ἁμαρτήσομαι ἐναντίον τοῦ Θεοῦ; Ἡνίκα δὲ ἐλάλει τῷ Ἰωσὴφ ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας, καὶ οὐχ ὑπήκουεν αὐτῇ καθεύδειν μετ' αὐτῆς, τοῦ συγγενέσθαι αὐτῇ. Ἐγένετο δὲ τοιαύτη τις ἡμέρα, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν Ἰωσὴφ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ποιεῖν τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐθεὶς ἦν τῶν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἔσω, καὶ ἐπεσπάσατο αὐτὸν τῶν ἱματίων, λέγουσα· Κοιμήθητι μετ' ἐμοῦ. Καὶ καταλιπὼν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῆς, ἔφυγε, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω. Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς εἶδεν ὅτι καταλιπὼν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῆς ἔφυγε καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω, ἐκάλεσε τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, λέγουσα· Ἴδετε, εἰσήγαγεν ἡμῖν παῖδα Ἑβραῖον, ἐμπαίζειν ἡμῖν. Εἰσῆλθε πρὸς μὲ, λέγων· Κοιμήθητι μετ' ἐμοῦ, καὶ ἐβόησα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ. Ἐν δὲ τῷ ἀκοῦσαι αὐτὸν, ὅτι ὕψωσα τὴν φωνήν μου καὶ ἐβόησα, καταλιπὼν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ παρ' ἐμοὶ ἔφυγε, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω.» Ὁρᾷς ὅπως τὸ μὲν γύναιον εἰς εὐνὴν, καὶ οὐχ ἑκόντα παρεβιάζετο, τῷ γεμὴν ἐρήρειστο πρὸς ἐγκράτειαν ὁ νοῦς ὑπ' οὐδενὸς τὸ σύμπαν ἡττώμενος; Βούπαις ἦν ἔτι, ἑπτακαίδεκά που μόλις ἐτῶν, ἐν πρώταις ὑπήνης ἐκβολαῖς, ἐν ἀκμαῖς ἡδονῶν, καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὅτι μάλιστα διαπύροις κινήμασι, καὶ ἵν' οὕτως εἴποιμεν, σκληραῖς καὶ ἀνουθετήτοις ἐπιθυμίαις. Φιλεῖ γὰρ ἀεί πως ἐν ἀθραύστοις ἔτι τοῦ ὀρεκτιᾷν ὁρμαῖς, τὸ ἔφ
pass_a_gloss: Cyril: If one goes to the celebrated Joseph himself, he will find him having let go nothing of uprightness, but having understood that God will work together with him toward anything at all and will come to his aid, if he should refuse outright the need to be defiled. For though it was possible to prosper and be broadened out in luxuries, letting himself go to run with the fiery leapings of youth toward the sweet and dear, and to be carried by unrebuked impulses, this he did not do, far from it; but he made, as it were, the portion with God the better, and set before the labors of self-control everything that fattens for the moment. For he knew that the provocation of the flesh is somehow sweet at the beginnings and as it were bewitches the mind with honey, as pleasure goes in these things, but at the end it turns down into what is no longer sweet; for penalties at once and punishments, and what not of such evils, will be hung down upon (fut. pass) the head of the one who has sinned. Do you wish we tell a few of the things written about him? Palladius: Certainly. Cyril: [Genesis 39:6b-15 LXX quoted: Joseph handsome in form and very beautiful in appearance; after these words his master's wife cast her eyes on him and said 'Sleep with me'; he would not; 'if my master because of me knows nothing in his house and has given all he has into my hands, and nothing in this house is above me, nor has anything been taken out from me except you, because you are his wife, how shall I do this evil word and sin before God?'; she spoke day after day and he did not obey her to sleep with her, to be with her; such a day came, he went in to do his works, none of the household inside; she drew him by his garments saying 'Sleep with me'; leaving his garments in her hands he fled and went outside; when she saw, she called those in the house: 'See, he brought in to us a Hebrew servant to mock us; he came in to me saying Sleep with me, and I cried out with a great voice; when he heard that I raised my voice, leaving his garments with me he fled and went out.'] Do you see how the little woman was forcing him, unwilling, toward a bed, but his mind had been propped firm toward self-control, worsted by nothing at all? He was still a big boy, barely about seventeen years, at the first sproutings of the beard, in the peaks of pleasures, in the most fiery movements, and so to say in hard and unadmonishable desires. For the adolescent kind is always somehow wont to be in still unbroken impulses of craving, and does not much endure the bridles toward self-control. [last clause runs across the PG column break into section 32]
pass_b_english: Cyril: And if one turns to the celebrated Joseph himself, he will find that Joseph neglected no part of uprightness, but understood that God would work with him in anything at all and come to his help, if he refused outright to let himself be defiled. For he could have prospered and given himself up to luxuries, letting himself run with the fiery leaps of youth toward whatever was sweet and dear, and be carried along by impulses that no one rebuked. This he did not do; far from it. Instead he reckoned the portion that is with God the better, as it were, and preferred the labors of self-control to everything that pampers for the moment. For he knew that the stirring of the flesh is somehow sweet at first and bewitches the mind as if with honey, so far as there is pleasure in such things; yet in the end it turns to what is no longer sweet. For at once penalties and punishments, and every evil of that kind, will hang over the head of the one who has sinned. Shall we recount a few of the things written about him?

Cyril: ‘And Joseph,’ it says, ‘was handsome in form and very beautiful in appearance. And after these things his master’s wife cast her eyes on Joseph and said, “Lie with me.” But he would not, and he said to his master’s wife, “If because of me my master knows nothing of what is in his house, and he has given into my hands all that he has, and nothing in this house is above me, and nothing has been kept back from me except you, because you are his wife, how then shall I do this evil thing and sin before God?” And as she spoke to Joseph day after day, he would not listen to her, to sleep with her and be with her. Then a certain day came, and Joseph went into the house to do his work, and none of the household was inside; and she caught hold of him by his garments, saying, “Lie with me.” And leaving his garments in her hands, he fled and went outside. And when she saw that he had left his garments in her hands and fled and gone outside, she called those who were in the house and spoke to them, saying, “See, he has brought in a Hebrew servant to us to make sport of us. He came in to me, saying, ‘Lie with me,’ and I cried out with a loud voice. And when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garments with me and fled and went outside.”’ (Genesis 39:6–15) You see how the wretched woman tried to force him to her bed against his will, yet his mind stood firm in self-control and was overcome by nothing at all? He was still a lad, only about seventeen years old (Genesis 37:2), with his first beard just coming, at the height of pleasure, amid the most fiery stirrings and, if we may put it so, amid hard desires that heed no warning. For youth is always somehow given to impulses of craving that are still unbroken, and it does not readily bear the bridles that lead to self-control.

choices.why: ἐννενοηκότα rendered as a second finding ('but understood'), not a causal 'for'; 'in everything whatever' -> 'in anything at all'
restored γάρ ('For he could have...'); κατευρύνεσθαι 'spread himself out' (calque) -> 'given himself up to luxuries'
LXX τοιαύτη τις ἡμέρα: 'such a day came' -> 'a certain day came'
βούπαις 'growing boy' -> 'lad'; που μόλις 'barely ... or so' -> 'only about'; ἐν ... ἐν stiff 'in the most fiery stirrings' -> 'amid'; σκληραῖς kept as 'hard'

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 14 exists to compare. Translated fresh from the Migne PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: Migne PG 68 print; the column break may cut a sentence or a word.

The Greek of this section breaks mid-word at the column change (τὸ ἔφ|ηβον); the whole closing sentence ('For youth is always somehow prone ... bridles that lead to self-control') is rendered here at the end of section 31, so section 32 begins with the next sentence. The quotation is Genesis 39:6b-15 LXX (it begins with the second half of verse 6, 'And Joseph was handsome in form'); English Bible numbering is the same. The LXX 'this evil word' (τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ πονηρόν) is rendered 'this evil thing', the Hebraism's sense. 'Seventeen years' is cited to Genesis 37:2 (Joseph's age when sold); Cyril applies it loosely ('barely about seventeen') to the time of the temptation. ἐπιείκεια rendered 'uprightness' (Cyril's general sense of virtuous conduct), not 'gentleness'. γενικῶς ('generally, in kind') taken as 'outright'. γύναιον is a contemptuous diminutive, rendered 'the wretched woman'. Uncited allusions: the honey that is sweet at first but not in the end recalls Proverbs 5:3-4 (the harlot's lips drip honey, afterward bitter), but the wording is not close enough to cite; 'the portion with God' may echo Luke 10:42 but uses μοῖρα, not μερίς, so no citation.
προετίθει + gen. rendered as preference: 'preferred the labors of self-control to everything that pampers'
checked Genesis 39:6b-15 LXX quotation clause by clause; Genesis 37:2 (age seventeen) confirmed
